**Terms**
- A **signal** is a Weave feature that scores agent turns and applies tags. It surfaces quality and safety issues, such as a frustrated user, and highlights the traces that need your attention [S1].
- A **turn** is one back-and-forth exchange between the user and the agent [S3].
- A **tag** is a label put on matching items, such as "user-frustration". A **rating** is a number from 0.0 to 1.0 [S3].

For your goal, you want a tag, not a rating.

**Set it up**
1. Go to Forge, select your project, and choose **Agents** in the sidebar. Then open the **Signals** tab [S2].
2. Select **+ New signal**. This opens the **Create signals** drawer, which lists **Tags** and **Ratings** [S5].
3. Under Tags, pick the preset **User Frustration**. It detects when the user shows signs of frustration, anger, confusion, or dissatisfaction [S6]. The preset's description names both confusion and anger or dissatisfaction, which matches "confused or annoyed".

**See the matches**
The **Signals** tab shows a table with one row per signal result. Useful columns are:
- **Scorer**: which signal produced the row.
- **Last message**: a preview of the scored turn's last message.
- **Agent**.
- **Scores**: shows the tag if matched.
- **When**: when it was scored.

You can narrow the table with the time window selector and the **Filter** bar, by scorer, agent, score range, or time period [S4]. That lets your team filter by scorer and work through the rows.

sources.text:
## Get started

To view signals for your project:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.
2. In the sidebar menu, select **Agents** to view all agent conversations saved for your project.
3. In the tab bar, select **Signals**.

![The Signals tab showing a list of scored turns for the agent.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/agent-view-signals.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=8c6cbeb0985f1892769e14cbf70fb16c)

# Monitor your agents with signals

> Use Weave signals to score agent turns, apply tags, and surface quality and safety issues in production.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

In Weave's [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md), the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. Signals surface quality and safety issues to flag problems, find patterns, and highlight the traces that need your attention. Use signals to automatically score the quality of your agent's responses, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content.

To score turns with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score agent turns with a remote scorer](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/remote-scorer-signals.md).

sources.text:
## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. The signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag, so a tag signal might run successfully even if you don't see any output.
* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

#### Tags presets

| Template | What it detects |
| - | - |
| **User Frustration** | User shows signs of frustration, anger, confusion, or dissatisfaction. |
| **Malicious Intent (Jailbreaking)** | User attempts to jailbreak the system, extract restricted content, perform prompt injection, use role-play exploits, or otherwise manipulate the agent into ignoring its guardrails. |

sources.heading: Signals table
sources.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

all_read_evidence.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

results.title: Monitor using built-in signals
results.heading: How signals work
results.snippet:
### How signals work

Each signal uses an LLM-as-a-judge approach to classify traces:

* **Trace selection**: Quality signals evaluate successful root-level traces. Error signals evaluate failed traces. Weave doesn't score child spans and intermediate Calls.
* **Prompt construction**: Weave constructs a prompt that includes the trace metadata, inputs, outputs, exception details (if any), and the operation's source code. Weave appends the signal's classifier prompt with instructions for the specific issue to detect.
* **LLM scoring**: For each signal, a Serverless Inference model performs a binary classification (whether that issue is present on the trace). Detected issues are returned as comma-delimited string tags (for example, `"Low-quality, User-frustration, Forgetful"`).

When multiple signals from the same group (Quality or Error) are active, Weave batches the signals into a single LLM call. The model evaluates all active classifiers in one pass and returns a result for each.

Weave accepts any OTel span and stores all of its attributes, but the Agents view renders spans that follow the [OTel GenAI semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md). result.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

**Short answer:** Set this up as a **signal** in your project's **Agents** view, on the **Signals** tab. You also see the matches there.

**Terms**
- A **signal** is an automatic scorer. It labels or rates your agent's conversations so you can find problems without reading every exchange [S1].
- A **turn** is one back-and-forth exchange between the user and the agent [S3].
- A **tag** is a label put on matching items, such as "user-frustration". A **rating** is a number from 0.0 to 1.0 [S3].

For your goal, you want a tag, not a rating.

**Set it up**
1. Go to Forge, select your project, and choose **Agents** in the sidebar. Then open the **Signals** tab [S2].
2. Select **+ New signal**. This opens the **Create signals** drawer, which lists **Tags** and **Ratings** [S5].
3. Under Tags, pick the preset **User Frustration**. It detects when the user shows signs of frustration, anger, confusion, or dissatisfaction [S6]. That covers both "confused" and "annoyed".

The docs also describe custom signals, which you could use if the preset isn't right. I didn't read that section, so I can't describe how to configure one.

**See the matches**
The **Signals** tab shows a table with one row per scored result. Useful columns are:
- **Scorer**: which signal produced the row.
- **Last message**: a preview of the scored turn's last message.
- **Agent**.
- **Scores**: shows the tag if matched.
- **When**: when it was scored.

You can narrow the table with the time window selector and the **Filter** bar (by scorer, agent, score range, or time period) [S4]. Your team can filter to the User Frustration scorer and work through the rows.

**Caveats**
- The Signals tab only shows rows for items that matched a tag. A tag signal can run fine and still show nothing [S5].
- If you expect matches and see none, open **Traces** in the project sidebar. Check the scorer name and the **Status** column. Scorer errors show a red indicator with details [S7].
- You can turn signals on or off, edit them, or delete them from the active-signals button in the toolbar [S8].
- The pages I read don't say whether a new signal scores conversations that were saved before you created it, or only new ones. Check this with a small test.
- Weave also has an older "Monitors" page, which describes a different workflow. I haven't mixed it into these steps.

**Next step:** Create the **User Frustration** tag signal, then check the Signals tab for rows with that scorer.
